notes: NYC Fair Workweek Law, retail (Admin. Code Title 20 ch. 12): covers businesses with 20+ employees primarily selling consumer goods at stores in NYC. Effective Nov. 26, 2017.
Violation of the 72-hour schedule notice may cost $300 per affected worker (DCWP FAQ).
No retail rest-between-shifts rule (NYC's clopening rule applies to fast food, out of scope).
Minimum wage effective date from Lab. Law § 652(1-a)(a); NYS DOL confirms the rate stays $17.00 on Jan. 1, 2027.

Fair Workweek retail (DCWP FAQ): schedules due 72 h ahead; within 72 h, cancelling or subtracting >15 min is prohibited (not a premium), adding a new shift or >15 min needs the employee's advance written consent after being told they may decline; on-call and 'check-in' shifts are prohibited. No predictability pay exists for retail. Allowed within 72 h: employee-requested time off, shift trades between employees, closures for emergencies.

Consent record must contain the date/time consent was given and reference the specific change; if extra time is added at the end of a shift, written consent may be obtained up to 15 minutes after the extra time begins. The FAQ does not say whether a text reply is a sufficient 'written' record (text_message_counts_as_written=false, conservative); the employer may transmit schedules by text.

Coverage: retail businesses primarily selling consumer goods with 20 or more employees across all NYC stores under common ownership or management (part-time/temporary included). Fast-food rules (premiums) are separate and not encoded (restaurant meals are not consumer goods).
applies_to='retail': the retail provisions cover stores selling consumer goods; restaurant meals are not consumer goods (DCWP FAQ). Fast food has separate rules, not encoded.

exemption_applies_to: written consent is required for any added time over 15 minutes within 72 h — 'adding a new shift or requiring an employee to report ... earlier or to end their shift ... after the scheduled end time' (DCWP FAQ).

consent_record_must_include: date and time the employee gave consent
the specific schedule or shift change (no general/ongoing consent)
params.exemption_note: Extra time within 72 h needs "the employee's advance written consent" after being told they may say no; the written record must "contain the date and time the employee gave consent" and reference the specific shift change.

rules.summary: NYC retail (20+ NYC store employees): no premium pay. Within 72 hours of a shift the employer may not cancel or cut it by more than 15 minutes, and may add more than 15 minutes only with the employee's advance written consent.

citation.title: NYC DCWP — Fair Workweek Law FAQs for Retail (4/1/2022)
citation.excerpt: A retail employer cannot require an employee to work more than 15 minutes of extra time unless the employee has at least 72 hours' advance notice ... must obtain the employee's advance written consent.

rules.summary: The minimum wage in New York City is $17.00 an hour from January 1, 2026 (unchanged on Jan. 1, 2027 per NYS DOL).

citation.title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 652(1-a)(a) — Minimum wage, New York City
citation.excerpt: every employer regardless of size shall pay to each of its employees for each hour worked in the city of New York a wage of not less than ... $17.00 on and after January 1, 2026
